# Expertise

## Methods

Alden's lab builds cross-species chromatin state annotations by aligning
regulatory regions across mammalian genomes and projecting a shared
chromatin-state model onto each species [alden2020atlas]. The resulting
reference atlas spans a dozen mammalian species and is maintained as a
versioned public resource.

## Intellectual lineage

This work extends single-species chromatin-state segmentation methods into
a comparative framework, motivated by the observation that regulatory
elements turn over far faster across evolutionary time than coding
sequence [alden2020atlas].

## Recurring critiques

A recurring position is that comparative epigenomic claims made from a
single reference species overstate how conserved a regulatory element
really is; true conservation claims require the multi-species atlas, not a
single liftover [alden2020atlas].

## Career trajectory

Early work focused on single-species chromatin segmentation; the atlas
project [alden2020atlas] began once cross-species alignment tools matured
enough to make comparative annotation tractable at scale.
